input.customer_message: @MicrosoftHelps It's definitely lasted well. It's only recently started hitting issues. I've planned to upgrade for a while now. I'm definitely gonna get another Surface as my next tablet, though. ^.^
input.conversation_context:
MICROSOFT (2582324): @220504 No worries. We'll keep an eye on your tweet.
CUSTOMER (2582325): @152402 I still haven't tried it yet. I'll let you know how it turns out!
CUSTOMER (2582326): @220504 Hi. We just wanted to know if the resolution we have provided resolved the battery notification discrepancy that you've experienced?
CUSTOMER (2582327): @152402 It hasn't fixed it, but I now think it's probably just the battery being old and not holding charge as well as it used to. To see if it had fixed it, I tried to run the battery right down...
CUSTOMER (2582328): @MicrosoftHelps my @123127 seems to have stopped giving me low battery warnings. It just runs down to 0% and shuts down suddenly. Where's the settings for this so I can turn the warnings back on?
MICROSOFT (2622401): @220504 er Yes, we have to consider that it's old that's why it doesn't hold as much charge back in the day and the sudden drop from 15% to 0% indicates the wear level where-in, the 15% charge doesn't last long as it used to. Have you installed the latest Windows update?
CUSTOMER (2622402): @MicrosoftHelps Yes. I have got the latest updates. It is pretty old for a tablet now as it's a Surface Pro, first generation.
CUSTOMER (2622403): @152402 ... it got down to 15%, then warned me of a low battery & immediately hibernated. I plugged it in, and woke it up, and the battery was suddenly showing 0% charge.
MICROSOFT (2622404): @220504 It's still a good thing that it function as it's supposed to aside from the battery, despite the fact that it was the first version. If you consider getting a new one, you can check the new line of Surface devices here: https://t.co/tFXPULxWPL
